description: Captures files stored under a configured Dropbox folder path and parses them into records.

credentialModes.name: Dropbox OAuth2 (client id + client secret + refresh token)

continuity.notes: No server-side state is created in the customer's Dropbox account: the connector only calls files/list_folder, files/list_folder/continue and files/download, all read-only. The Dropbox listing cursor DOES exist but is purely intra-call: List() drains every page in one loop (`for f.HasMore { ListFolderContinue(f.Cursor) }`) and the cursor is discarded when List() returns. It is never written into a Flow checkpoint, so a cursor cannot expire between syncs and there is no cursor-invalidation resume window. Cross-sync resume is instead carried entirely by filesource's own checkpoint: an exclusive modification-time window (MinBound advanced to the sweep's MaxMod, MaxBound = now - 30s via TimeHorizonDelta) plus a lexicographic `Path` marker, both of which are durable and time-independent. Consequence: pausing arbitrarily long is safe for resumability, but every sweep re-fetches the entire folder listing from Dropbox because StartAt is applied client-side after the pages are fetched.

discovery.method: Single binding synthesized from the configured endpoint path (no enumeration of the account)
discovery.querySketch: Discover() returns exactly one binding: RecommendedName = config.path with leading/trailing '/' trimmed, resource = {stream: config.path}, key = [/_meta/file, /_meta/offset], document schema = x-infer-schema minimal _meta schema. Connectivity is proven separately by a files/list_folder call on config.path with Limit=1.
excludes: FolderMetadata entries when the listing is recursive
DeletedMetadata and all other metadata types

backfill.listing: Identical mechanism to the incremental leg; the first sweep is simply the one where the checkpointed MinBound is the zero time, so no object is excluded by the lower modification-time bound. MaxBound is still now-30s, so objects modified in the last 30 seconds are deferred to the next sweep.

incremental.listing: files/list_folder{Path: prefix, Recursive: true}, then repeatedly files/list_folder/continue{Cursor: previous response Cursor} while HasMore. All pages are drained inside a single List() call and the cursor is then thrown away (never checkpointed). Dropbox returns entries ordered by modification time, so the connector converts FileMetadata to {path_lower, content_hash, size, server_modified}, drops entries where !(StartAt < path), and re-sorts the whole set lexicographically by path before handing it to filesource, which requires monotonic path order. Resume across sweeps is therefore NOT cursor-based: it is (a) the checkpointed lexicographic `Path` used as StartAt, applied client-side after the full listing has already been fetched, and (b) an exclusive server_modified window MinBound < modTime < MaxBound, where MaxBound = now-30s and MinBound advances to the sweep's MaxMod on completion (unless advanced.ascendingKeys is set, in which case MinBound is never advanced and progress is carried by `Path` alone).

authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode is offered and its three fields — client_id, client_secret and refresh_token — are all required by both the JSON schema and credentials.validate(). There is no API-key/access-token path and no client_credentials path: getOauthClient builds an oauth2.Config from the user's own client id/secret and seeds a token with only a RefreshToken and Expiry=now, forcing an immediate refresh. Standalone, that means the user registers their own Dropbox app AND obtains a long-lived refresh token, i.e. T3. Estuary's hosted control plane hides this: the config schema carries `x-oauth2-provider: dropbox` and oauth2Spec() supplies the authorize/token templates (token_access_type=offline, response_type=code, AccessTokenResponseJsonMap extracting /refresh_token), so in the Web UI Estuary's own registered app performs the authorization_code exchange and injects all three values. The tier that matters for a standalone integration is still T3_BYO_REFRESH.

unionMisfits.description: The objectStore `store` enum has no `dropbox` member. Dropbox is a consumer/business file-sync service reached over its own HTTPS RPC API (api.dropboxapi.com / content.dropboxapi.com via the dropbox-sdk-go-unofficial v6 SDK), not S3/GCS/Azure/SFTP/SharePoint/Drive. `drive` is the nearest neighbour but is factually wrong.

The PullSpec `objects` shape has no place to record that the listing pagination is a stateful server cursor that is deliberately NOT persisted, nor that the resume marker (StartAt) is applied client-side after the full listing was already fetched. These are different cost/correctness profiles that the current single `listing` string can only capture as prose.

There is no schedule anywhere in the connector. filesource.Pull performs exactly ONE sweep per binding and then returns, so the process exits and re-invocation cadence is owned entirely by the Flow runtime. The schema has no way to say 'scheduling is delegated to the host runtime' as distinct from 'unknown'.

proposedShape.description: one bounded sweep per connector invocation; cadence set by the runtime

unionMisfits.description: Backfill and incremental are literally the same code path; they differ only by the value of the checkpointed MinBound (zero vs. previous MaxMod). Emitting two near-identical PullSpecs overstates the distinction.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Nothing in source-dropbox or filesource sets a poll interval, cron, or sleep. filesource.Pull launches one sweep per binding and returns when the errgroup completes, so the connector process ends after a single pass and the re-invocation cadence lives in the Flow runtime, which is outside this repo's connector code. Recording an interval would be invention.
abstained.streams[0].schedules: Same reason as execution.defaultSchedule: bindings carry no schedule field at all (the resource spec is only {stream, syncMode, namespace, cursorField}, and syncMode/namespace/cursorField are hidden with jsonschema:"-").
abstained.streams[0].cursorField: The incremental bound is Dropbox's server_modified timestamp on the object metadata plus a lexicographic path marker, both held in connector checkpoint state. Neither is a field of the emitted documents (documents carry only /_meta/file and /_meta/offset plus inferred payload fields), so there is no record-level cursor field to name.
abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl: The objectStore transport variant has no baseUrl member, and the connector never names a host: the endpoints are whatever dropbox-sdk-go-unofficial/v6 uses internally (dropbox.Config is constructed with only an http.Client).
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.authUrl: Reported as the base authorize endpoint parsed out of AUTH_URL_TEMPLATE_FORMAT_STR; the literal in the source is a mustache template carrying token_access_type=offline, client_id, response_type=code, redirect_uri, state and scope query parameters, not a bare URL.
abstained.streams[0].pull.incremental.paginator: Not applicable — the PullSpec kind here is `objects`, not `http`. The listing's own cursor/HasMore pagination is described in `listing` instead; it would map to type cursor / tokenFrom body / tokenTo body_field / terminateOn envelope_flag if the schema allowed a paginator on an objects PullSpec.
